title: Chat C — G2 DB materials and inter-material relations
status: Bounded static contract; no DB runtime equivalence claim

scope.included: Record selection/stride, append ordering, IDs versus one-based positions, ordered relation keys, raw scalar and table transfers, direct nested deserializers, reset ownership and partial mutations.
scope.existing_evidence: Retained material/relation KEY contracts supply structural ownership and table storage facts only. Their runtime comparisons are not DB-import validation.

rules: The field map preserves506 material and160 relation write occurrences, including constants and repeated conditional destinations, plus80 material/15 relation deserializer call sites. Counts are statement occurrences, not unique semantic fields.

Every row binds a parent evidence ID, exact pseudocode statement and one-based line after CR removal. Destination offsets are bytes. Guard context and nearest aliases are navigation aids; full saved pseudocode governs branching and order.

Material param_1 is int*: param_1[index] and param_1+index use4-byte strides, including casted double stores. Relation param_1 is a byte address. Do not copy decompiler indices directly into model byte offsets.

Material reader dossier body spans14028f300..140294a03,22,276 bytes; complete39,776-code-unit pseudocode and3,301 assembly rows retained. High p-code is truncated, so cross-operation value-flow completeness is not claimed.
Relation reader has provider-reported noncontiguous ranges140336740..1403367a3 and1403367a6..140337ef7. Preserve the two-byte gap and provider body scope; don't claim recovered original source.

relation.formula: For outer material ordinal i and inner ordinal j: record=A+(R[2]-1+(j*n+i)*R[142])*8. Appended relation list ordinal is i*n+j when all n material lookups succeed. Thus storage order differs from traversal order.
relation.pairs: Keys are material[i].ID then material[j].ID, not i/j, not sorted IDs and not canonicalized unordered pairs. All ordered pairs, including self-pairs, are appended. No exact-key lookup/deduplication is called here.

First pass appends/deserializes all n materials and records each resulting ID in temporary n-int32 array. Second pass obtains material ordinal i+1; for mode exactly1, replaces each reference position r with tempIDs[r-1]. No range check is visible.

After freeing temporary IDs,1d6250 visits materials by insertion position. For each source still in mode1, it searches each referenced ID. If target exists and target mode!=2, it frees/zeros target refs only when target count>0, then sets target mode2.

This pass is order-sensitive: a target can lose its own outgoing references before its turn. Self-reference can clear the source count during its loop. Duplicate IDs make later exact-ID reconciliation target the first matching ID, despite earlier positional translation.
Do not implement references as direct IDs at initial decode, a sorted-ID rank, a simultaneous graph closure, or a deduplicated material dictionary without an explicit integration decision.

gaps.question: Which physical properties, units, interpolation rules and scientific meanings belong to these offset/code fields?
gaps.impact: Keep raw IDs,codes,bit patterns andbranches; no semantic names or unit conversions invented.

gaps.impact: Full3D v11000 indexbindings only; dimension/version branches recorded but not a support claim.

proposed_tests.scenario: Nonsequential material IDs [17,-4,90] and distinct record sentinels
proposed_tests.expected: Verify stored strides and material order. Nine relation list entries must read matrix positions [0,3,6,1,4,7,2,5,8], including self-pairs.

proposed_tests.scenario: Duplicate, zero and negative material IDs
proposed_tests.expected: Every DB record appends. Position-to-ID translation preserves duplicates; later exact-ID lookup finds the first match.

proposed_tests.scenario: Forward, backward, self and cyclic references
proposed_tests.expected: Translate every position before reconciliation. Verify target reference clearing and order-sensitive source modes, including self-reference loop termination.

proposed_tests.scenario: Reference count zero or positive; valid and invalid keys/positions
proposed_tests.expected: Zero count preserves constructor state. Define safe adapter rejection for invalid keys or positions separately from native faults.

proposed_tests.scenario: Material counts 0,1,3 and unrelated cached relation counts
proposed_tests.expected: Iteration uses n*n, retains inactive entries and preserves the imported cached counter.

proposed_tests.scenario: Relation Z0 zero, positive and negative
proposed_tests.expected: Zero writes mode/active only. Nonzero, including negative, enters the active branch and preserves mutation order.

proposed_tests.scenario: Material Q11 modes0..16, unknown positives and negative fractions
proposed_tests.expected: Check mode mapping, coefficient copies, table keys and the negative-real override after the truncated switch.

proposed_tests.scenario: Common material table selectors0,1,2,3 and unknown values
proposed_tests.expected: Check constants, keys, axes and counts. Unknown selectors can retain constructor shape and still invoke a reader.

proposed_tests.scenario: Material Q53, Q57 and Q70 mode branches
proposed_tests.expected: Verify negative codes, coefficient runs and table shape/key sources without assigning scientific meanings.
Check B+7d8 and version-tail gates in both dimensions, including safe handling of unguarded typed-table keys.

proposed_tests.scenario: Multi-axis tables selected by Q139,Q141,Q143,Q145
proposed_tests.expected: True read flags consume leading counts; false flags do not. Diagnostics do not imply rollback.

proposed_tests.scenario: Q65 indirect width20 record, tags0,5 and other
proposed_tests.expected: Check mode, constant, nested key/count fields and temporary cleanup. Reject invalid payloads under the proposed adapter policy.

proposed_tests.scenario: Nested material Q109 modes0,1,2,3,4,5 and negative
proposed_tests.expected: Verify nine concatenated tables, five ordered lists, cursor advances and diagnostic-only count mismatch.

proposed_tests.scenario: Nested coefficient counts-1,0,12,13 and table shapes0..3
proposed_tests.expected: Only upper count clamps to12. Verify W23/W24/W37, skip-byte state and130290 cursor formulas; scalar131e30 calls are no-ops.

proposed_tests.scenario: Relation Z6 modes1..13/default and Z13 submodes
proposed_tests.expected: Verify widths, shapes, trailer reads, direct coefficient runs, count formulas and mode aliases.

proposed_tests.scenario: Relation optional flags and simple table selectors
proposed_tests.expected: Skipped subobjects retain defaults; verify scalar0/4 special case and exact two-axis count slots.

proposed_tests.scenario: 64-byte material names and80-byte relation names
proposed_tests.expected: Verify full eight-byte transformation, trailing trim, embedded NUL, leading spaces and all-space behavior; no G1 blank-row normalization.

proposed_tests.scenario: Typed marker10 and legacy table ranks0,1,2,3
proposed_tests.expected: Verify header offsets, key gates and ownership.131e30 handles only ranks1/2; rank3 copying occurs through other readers, not this dispatcher.

proposed_tests.scenario: Repeated imports A->A and A->B->A, same/changed dimension
proposed_tests.expected: Collections are destroyed before each DB import. New materials use ordered unit initialization; G1 scalar-control retention remains separate.

proposed_tests.scenario: Failure after initial material/reference/relation mutations
proposed_tests.expected: Record partial native state. Adapter rejection and atomicity are separate design decisions.

proposed_tests.scenario: Candidate freeze followed by independent held-out DB fixtures
proposed_tests.expected: Compare IDs,modes,counts,table contents and raw64 bits, not heap addresses. Report branch coverage and exclude scientific claims.
